```python
"""Deploy gate for the published Atlas web data (design 2026-10-07 §C.1.5)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import gzip
import hashlib
import json
import threading
import urllib.request
from collections.abc import Iterator
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import unquote, urlsplit

import pytest

from genomeos.publication.web_layout import IMMUTABLE_CACHE_CONTROL, PRODUCTION_ORIGINS
from scripts import check_atlas_web_data as gate
from tests.atlas_web_fixtures import GNOMAD_KEY, object_bytes, staged_catalog, write_dist

BUCKET = "example-bucket"


@dataclass
class FakeBucket:
    """storage.googleapis.com in miniature: path-style object reads plus the JSON metadata API."""

    objects: dict[str, bytes]  # catalog key -> decoded bytes
    allowed_origins: set[str] = field(default_factory=lambda: set(PRODUCTION_ORIGINS))
    headers: dict[str, dict[str, str | None]] = field(default_factory=dict)  # key -> overrides; None drops
    metadata: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = field(default_factory=dict)  # key -> custom-metadata overrides
    bodies: dict[str, bytes] = field(default_factory=dict)  # key -> stored gzip body override
    missing: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
    unavailable_once: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)  # first request answers 503

    def key_for(self, name: str) -> str | None:
        prefix = "atlas/web/"
        key = name[len(prefix) :] if name.startswith(prefix) else None
        return key if key in self.objects and key not in self.missing else None

    def stored(self, key: str) -> bytes:
        return self.bodies.get(key, gzip.compress(self.objects[key], compresslevel=9, mtime=0))


def _handler(bucket: FakeBucket) -> type[BaseHTTPRequestHandler]:
    class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
        def log_message(self, format: str, *args: object) -> None:
            return

        def do_HEAD(self) -> None:
            self._object(send_body=False)

        def do_GET(self) -> None:
            path = urlsplit(self.path).path
            api = f"/storage/v1/b/{BUCKET}/o/"
            if path.startswith(api):
                self._metadata(unquote(path[len(api) :]))
            else:
                self._object(send_body=True)

        def _reply(self, status: int, headers: dict[str, str | None], body: bytes, length: int) -> None:
            self.send_response(status)
            for name, value in headers.items():
                if value is not None:
                    self.send_header(name, value)
            self.send_header("Content-Length", str(length))
            self.end_headers()
            if body:
                self.wfile.write(body)

        def _object(self, *, send_body: bool) -> None:
            path = unquote(urlsplit(self.path).path)
            prefix = f"/{BUCKET}/"
            key = bucket.key_for(path[len(prefix) :]) if path.startswith(prefix) else None
            if key is None:
                self._reply(404, {}, b"", 0)
                return
            if key in bucket.unavailable_once:
                bucket.unavailable_once.discard(key)
                self._reply(503, {}, b"", 0)
                return
            stored = bucket.stored(key)
            accepts_gzip = "gzip" in (self.headers.get("Accept-Encoding") or "")
            body = stored if accepts_gzip else gzip.decompress(stored)
            headers: dict[str, str | None] = {
                "Cache-Control": IMMUTABLE_CACHE_CONTROL,
                "Content-Type": "application/octet-stream" if key.endswith(".gosa") else "application/json",
                "Content-Encoding": "gzip" if accepts_gzip else None,
                "Vary": "Origin",
                "x-goog-meta-sha256": hashlib.sha256(bucket.objects[key]).hexdigest(),
            }
            origin = self.headers.get("Origin")
            if origin is not None and origin in bucket.allowed_origins:
                headers["Access-Control-Allow-Origin"] = origin
            headers.update(bucket.headers.get(key, {}))
            self._reply(200, headers, body if send_body else b"", len(body))

        def _metadata(self, name: str) -> None:
            key = bucket.key_for(name)
            if key is None:
                body = b'{"error":{"code":404}}'
                self._reply(404, {"Content-Type": "application/json"}, body, len(body))
                return
            overrides = bucket.headers.get(key, {})
            resource = {
                "size": str(len(bucket.stored(key))),
                "contentEncoding": overrides.get("Content-Encoding", "gzip"),
                "cacheControl": overrides.get("Cache-Control", IMMUTABLE_CACHE_CONTROL),
                "crc32c": "AAAAAA==",
                "metadata": {
                    "sha256": hashlib.sha256(bucket.objects[key]).hexdigest(),
                    "decoded-bytes": str(len(bucket.objects[key])),
                    **bucket.metadata.get(key, {}),
                },
            }
            body = json.dumps(resource).encode()
            self._reply(200, {"Content-Type": "application/json"}, body, len(body))

    return Handler


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Served:
    bucket: FakeBucket
    base: str
    api_root: str


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def _no_proxies(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    """The fake bucket is on 127.0.0.1; never route test requests through an environment proxy."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(gate, "_OPENER", urllib.request.build_opener(urllib.request.ProxyHandler({})))
    monkeypatch.setattr(gate, "RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS", 0.0)


@pytest.fixture()
def served() -> Iterator[Served]:
    fake = FakeBucket(objects=object_bytes(staged_catalog()))
    server = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), _handler(fake))
    thread = threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
    thread.start()
    root = f"http://127.0.0.1:{server.server_address[1]}/"
    try:
        yield Served(fake, f"{root}{BUCKET}/atlas/web/", f"{root}storage/v1/")
    finally:
        server.shutdown()
        server.server_close()


def _run(served: Served, tmp_path: Path, *extra: str, base: str | None = None, dist: Path | None = None) -> int:
    catalog_path = tmp_path / "catalog.json"
    catalog_path.write_text(json.dumps(staged_catalog()), encoding="utf-8")
    site = write_dist(tmp_path / "dist", served.base) if dist is None else dist
    return gate.main(
        [
            "--catalog", str(catalog_path),
            "--base", served.base if base is None else base,
            "--bucket", BUCKET,
            "--dist", str(site),
            "--api-root", served.api_root,
            *extra,
        ]
    )


def test_a_correctly_published_bucket_passes_without_comparing_content_length(served: Served, tmp_path: Path, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]) -> None:
    assert _run(served, tmp_path, "--production") == 0
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.strip() == "ok: 6 artifact objects x 2 origins, 3 checked end to end, 2 site files"
    render = staged_catalog()["artifacts"][0]["web"]["render"]["url"]
    assert len(served.bucket.stored(render)) != len(served.bucket.objects[render])  # CL is the gzip size


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "base",
    ["", "/data/atlas/", "https://storage.googleapis.com/example-bucket/atlas/web", "http://127.0.0.1:9/example-bucket/elsewhere/"],
)
def test_an_empty_relative_or_malformed_base_fails(served: Served, tmp_path: Path, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str], base: str) -> None:
    assert _run(served, tmp_path, base=base) == 1
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.startswith("FAIL ")


def test_an_edge_base_must_name_the_checked_bucket(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    base = "https://storage.googleapis.com/example-other/atlas/web/"
    problems = gate.run_checks(staged_catalog(), base=base, bucket=BUCKET, dist=tmp_path, production=False)
    assert problems == [
        f"artifact base {base!r} does not serve bucket 'example-bucket' "
        "(expected https://storage.googleapis.com/example-bucket/atlas/web/)"
    ]


def test_a_production_build_that_did_not_bake_the_base_fails(served: Served, tmp_path: Path, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]) -> None:
    dist = write_dist(tmp_path / "same-origin", "/data/atlas/")
    assert _run(served, tmp_path, "--production", dist=dist) == 1
    assert "bakes artifact base '/data/atlas/'" in capsys.readouterr().out
    assert _run(served, tmp_path, dist=dist) == 0  # validate builds never bake the bucket base (§C.1.4)


def test_a_production_build_that_inlines_another_catalog_fails(served: Served, tmp_path: Path, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]) -> None:
    # The browser fetches the keys of the catalog dist inlines, so checking a different --catalog
    # would pass a build whose objects are not in the bucket.
    other = {**staged_catalog(), "artifacts": []}
    dist = write_dist(tmp_path / "other-catalog", served.base, catalog=other)
    assert _run(served, tmp_path, "--production", dist=dist) == 1
    assert "inlines a catalog that differs from --catalog" in capsys.readouterr().out
    assert _run(served, tmp_path, dist=dist) == 0  # only the production build job checks it


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("header", "value", "message"),
    [
        ("Content-Encoding", None, "Content-Encoding None, expected 'gzip'"),
        ("Cache-Control", "public, max-age=600", "Cache-Control 'public, max-age=600'"),
    ],
)
def test_transport_headers_are_required_on_every_object(served: Served, tmp_path: Path, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str], header: str, value: str | None, message: str) -> None:
    key = next(iter(served.bucket.objects))  # the manifest download: not on the critical path
    served.bucket.headers[key] = {header: value}
    assert _run(served, tmp_path) == 1
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert f"FAIL {key} (Origin https://genome-os.org): {message}" in out


def test_every_production_origin_needs_a_cors_grant(served: Served, tmp_path: Path, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]) -> None:
    served.bucket.allowed_origins.discard("https://www.genome-os.org")
    assert _run(served, tmp_path) == 1
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert "(Origin https://www.genome-os.org): Access-Control-Allow-Origin None" in out
    assert "(Origin https://genome-os.org): Access-Control-Allow-Origin" not in out


def test_metadata_must_carry_the_catalog_digest(served: Served, tmp_path: Path, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]) -> None:
    key = next(iter(served.bucket.objects))
    served.bucket.metadata[key] = {"sha256": "0" * 64}
    assert _run(served, tmp_path) == 1
    assert f"FAIL {key}: metadata sha256 '{'0' * 64}'" in capsys.readouterr().out


def test_decoded_bytes_are_checked_only_where_the_catalog_declares_them(served: Served, tmp_path: Path, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]) -> None:
    ref = staged_catalog()["artifacts"][0]

    assert _run(served, tmp_path) == 0

def test_the_default_artifact_is_checked_end_to_end(served: Served, tmp_path: Path, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]) -> None:
    render = staged_catalog()["artifacts"][0]["web"]["render"]["url"]

def test_a_missing_object_fails(served: Served, tmp_path: Path, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]) -> None:

- [ ] Step 3: Implement `scripts/check_atlas_web_data.py`.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Deploy gate for the Atlas web data in the public bucket (fast-load/GCS design 2026-10-07 §C.1.5).

Fails when the artifact base is empty or not absolute. For every artifact-base key in the catalog
(``grids.*.url``, ``web.render.url``, ``web.detail.url``, ``surface_url``, ``observations_url``,
``downloads.*.url``) it sends HEAD with ``Accept-Encoding: gzip`` and an ``Origin`` for each
production origin and requires 200, ``Content-Encoding: gzip``, the immutable ``Cache-Control`` and
``Access-Control-Allow-Origin`` echoing the origin or ``*``. From the public JSON API
(``storage/v1/b/<bucket>/o/<object>?fields=size,contentEncoding,cacheControl,metadata,crc32c``,
anonymous) it requires metadata ``sha256`` equal to the catalog digest and ``decoded-bytes`` equal to
the declared decoded size where one is declared. It never compares ``Content-Length`` with decoded
bytes: GCS reports the stored gzip size. It GETs, gunzips and sha256-checks the default artifact's
grid, render tier and observations, and checks that every site-base key (Natural Earth context and
external caches) exists in ``dist/``. ``--production`` (the Pages ``build`` job) also requires
``dist/app/index.html`` to bake exactly ``--base`` and to inline exactly ``--catalog``: the browser
fetches the inlined catalog's keys, so checking any other catalog proves nothing about the build.

Metadata is what the publisher asserts; it is trusted only because keys are content-addressed,
uploads refuse overwrite and publishing verifies the uploaded bytes (scripts/publish_atlas_web.py).
Standard library only, so CI needs no install.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import gzip
import hashlib
import json
import re
import sys
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
import zlib
from collections.abc import Iterable, Mapping, Sequence
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any
from urllib.parse import quote, urlsplit

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
if str(ROOT) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))

from genomeos.publication.web_layout import (  # noqa: E402
    IMMUTABLE_CACHE_CONTROL,
    OBJECT_PREFIX,
    PRODUCTION_ORIGINS,
    WebLayoutError,
    WebObject,
    artifact_objects,
    assert_absolute_data_base,
    assert_bucket_name,
    critical_objects,
    object_name,
    resolve_key,
    site_objects,
)

JSON_API_ROOT = "https://storage.googleapis.com/storage/v1/"
METADATA_FIELDS = "size,contentEncoding,cacheControl,metadata,crc32c"
TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 30
ATTEMPTS = 3
RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS = 1.0
WORKERS = 8
_DATA_BASES = re.compile(r'<script[^>]*\bid="atlas-data-bases"[^>]*>([^<]*)</script>')
# The build escapes every `<` in the inline catalog (escapeInlineJson), so `[^<]*` spans all of it.
_INLINE_CATALOG = re.compile(r'<script[^>]*\bid="atlas-catalog"[^>]*>([^<]*)</script>')
_OPENER = urllib.request.build_opener()


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Reply:
    status: int  # 0 when no HTTP response arrived
    headers: Mapping[str, str]  # lower-cased names
    body: bytes


def _lower(items: Iterable[tuple[str, str]]) -> dict[str, str]:
    return {name.lower(): value for name, value in items}


def fetch(url: str, *, method: str = "GET", headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None) -> Reply:
    """One request, retried on 5xx and connection errors; a 4xx is an answer, not an error."""
    request = urllib.request.Request(url, method=method, headers=dict(headers or {}))
    reply = Reply(0, {}, b"")
    for attempt in range(ATTEMPTS):
        if attempt:
            time.sleep(RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS * attempt)
        try:
            with _OPENER.open(request, timeout=TIMEOUT_SECONDS) as response:
                return Reply(response.status, _lower(response.headers.items()), response.read())
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
            reply = Reply(error.code, _lower(error.headers.items()), error.read())
            if error.code < 500:
                return reply
        except (urllib.error.URLError, TimeoutError, ConnectionError) as error:
            reply = Reply(0, {}, str(error).encode())
    return reply


def check_serving(item: WebObject, base: str, origins: Sequence[str]) -> list[str]:
    url = resolve_key(item.key, base)
    problems: list[str] = []
    for origin in origins:
        where = f"{item.key} (Origin {origin})"
        reply = fetch(url, method="HEAD", headers={"Accept-Encoding": "gzip", "Origin": origin})
        if reply.status != 200:
            problems.append(f"{where}: HEAD {url} returned {reply.status}")
            continue
        encoding = reply.headers.get("content-encoding")
        if encoding != "gzip":
            problems.append(f"{where}: Content-Encoding {encoding!r}, expected 'gzip'")
        cache = reply.headers.get("cache-control")
        if cache != IMMUTABLE_CACHE_CONTROL:
            problems.append(f"{where}: Cache-Control {cache!r}, expected {IMMUTABLE_CACHE_CONTROL!r}")
        allowed = reply.headers.get("access-control-allow-origin")
        if allowed not in (origin, "*"):
            problems.append(f"{where}: Access-Control-Allow-Origin {allowed!r}, expected {origin!r} or '*'")
    return problems


def check_metadata(item: WebObject, bucket: str, api_root: str) -> list[str]:
    name = quote(object_name(item.key), safe="")
    url = f"{api_root}b/{quote(bucket, safe='')}/o/{name}?fields={METADATA_FIELDS}"
    reply = fetch(url, headers={"Accept-Encoding": "identity"})
    if reply.status != 200:
        return [f"{item.key}: JSON API returned {reply.status}"]
    try:
        resource: Any = json.loads(reply.body)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        return [f"{item.key}: JSON API returned a body that is not JSON"]
    metadata = resource.get("metadata") or {}
    problems: list[str] = []
    if metadata.get("sha256") != item.sha256:
        problems.append(f"{item.key}: metadata sha256 {metadata.get('sha256')!r}, catalog {item.sha256}")
    if item.decoded_bytes is not None and metadata.get("decoded-bytes") != str(item.decoded_bytes):
        problems.append(
            f"{item.key}: metadata decoded-bytes {metadata.get('decoded-bytes')!r}, "
            f"catalog declares {item.decoded_bytes}"
        )
    if resource.get("contentEncoding") != "gzip":
        problems.append(f"{item.key}: stored contentEncoding {resource.get('contentEncoding')!r}, expected 'gzip'")
    if resource.get("cacheControl") != IMMUTABLE_CACHE_CONTROL:
        problems.append(f"{item.key}: stored cacheControl {resource.get('cacheControl')!r}")
    return problems


def check_end_to_end(item: WebObject, base: str) -> list[str]:
    url = resolve_key(item.key, base)
    reply = fetch(url, headers={"Accept-Encoding": "gzip", "Origin": PRODUCTION_ORIGINS[0]})
    if reply.status != 200:
        return [f"{item.key}: GET {url} returned {reply.status}"]
    if reply.headers.get("content-encoding") != "gzip":
        return [f"{item.key}: GET Content-Encoding {reply.headers.get('content-encoding')!r}, expected 'gzip'"]
    try:
        data = gzip.decompress(reply.body)
    except (OSError, EOFError, zlib.error) as error:
        return [f"{item.key}: GET body is not gzip ({error})"]
    problems: list[str] = []
    digest = hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
    if digest != item.sha256:
        problems.append(f"{item.key}: decoded sha256 {digest}, catalog {item.sha256}")
    if item.decoded_bytes is not None and len(data) != item.decoded_bytes:
        problems.append(f"{item.key}: decoded {len(data)} bytes, catalog declares {item.decoded_bytes}")
    return problems


def check_site(dist: Path, catalog: Mapping[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
    site = dist / "data" / "atlas"
    problems: list[str] = []
    for item in site_objects(catalog):
        path = site / item.key
        if not path.is_file():
            problems.append(f"site-base {item.key}: missing from {site}")
            continue
        if item.sha256 is not None:
            digest = hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
            if digest != item.sha256:
                problems.append(f"site-base {item.key}: sha256 {digest}, catalog {item.sha256}")
    return problems


def baked_artifact_base(dist: Path) -> str | None:
    path = dist / "app" / "index.html"
    if not path.is_file():
        return None
    match = _DATA_BASES.search(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return None if match is None else str(json.loads(match.group(1))["artifact"])


def inlined_catalog(dist: Path) -> Any:
    """The catalog dist/app/index.html inlines (what the browser fetches by), or None."""
    path = dist / "app" / "index.html"
    if not path.is_file():
        return None
    match = _INLINE_CATALOG.search(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return None if match is None else json.loads(match.group(1))


def run_checks(
    catalog: Mapping[str, Any],
    *,
    base: str,
    bucket: str,
    dist: Path,
    production: bool,
    api_root: str = JSON_API_ROOT,
    origins: Sequence[str] = PRODUCTION_ORIGINS,
) -> list[str]:
    try:
        assert_absolute_data_base(base)
        assert_bucket_name(bucket)
    except WebLayoutError as error:
        return [str(error)]
    if not base.endswith(f"/{OBJECT_PREFIX}"):
        return [f"artifact base {base!r} must end in /{OBJECT_PREFIX}, the prefix the metadata check reads"]
    parts = urlsplit(base)
    if parts.hostname == "storage.googleapis.com" and parts.path != f"/{bucket}/{OBJECT_PREFIX}":
        return [
            f"artifact base {base!r} does not serve bucket {bucket!r} "
            f"(expected https://storage.googleapis.com/{bucket}/{OBJECT_PREFIX})"
        ]
    problems: list[str] = []
    if production:
        baked = baked_artifact_base(dist)
        if baked != base:
            problems.append(
                f"dist/app/index.html bakes artifact base {baked!r}, not {base!r}: the production build ran "
                "without PUBLIC_ATLAS_DATA_BASE_URL"
            )
        if inlined_catalog(dist) != catalog:
            problems.append(
                "dist/app/index.html inlines a catalog that differs from --catalog: the browser fetches "
                "the inlined catalog's keys, so build with ATLAS_CATALOG_PATH set to the checked catalog"
            )
    objects = artifact_objects(catalog)
    critical = critical_objects(catalog)
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=WORKERS) as pool:
        serving = list(pool.map(lambda item: check_serving(item, base, origins), objects))
        metadata = list(pool.map(lambda item: check_metadata(item, bucket, api_root), objects))
        end_to_end = list(pool.map(lambda item: check_end_to_end(item, base), critical))
    for found in [*serving, *metadata, *end_to_end]:
        problems.extend(found)
    problems.extend(check_site(dist, catalog))
    return problems


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Refuse a deploy whose Atlas web data is not published correctly.")
    parser.add_argument("--catalog", type=Path, required=True, help="the catalog the site inlines")
    parser.add_argument("--base", required=True, help="PUBLIC_ATLAS_DATA_BASE_URL (absolute, ends in atlas/web/)")
    parser.add_argument("--bucket", required=True, help="the ATLAS_DATA_BUCKET value")
    parser.add_argument("--dist", type=Path, required=True, help="the built site")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--production",
        action="store_true",
        help="also require dist to bake --base and to inline exactly --catalog (build job)",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--api-root", default=JSON_API_ROOT, help=argparse.SUPPRESS)
    return parser


def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    try:
        catalog = json.loads(args.catalog.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        problems = run_checks(
            catalog, base=args.base, bucket=args.bucket, dist=args.dist, production=args.production,
            api_root=args.api_root,
        )
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, WebLayoutError) as error:
        problems = [f"cannot check {args.catalog}: {error!r}"]
        catalog = {}
    if problems:
        for problem in problems:
            print(f"FAIL {problem}")
        print(
            f"FAILED: {len(problems)} problem(s); do not deploy until the bucket serves every object the "
            "catalog names (design 2026-10-07 §C.1.5)",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 1
    print(
        f"ok: {len(artifact_objects(catalog))} artifact objects x {len(PRODUCTION_ORIGINS)} origins, "
        f"{len(critical_objects(catalog))} checked end to end, {len(site_objects(catalog))} site files"
    )
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { mkdtempSync, readFileSync, rmSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import path from 'node:path';

import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';

import { artifactDataBaseFrom } from '../src/lib/data-url';

const websiteRoot = path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, '..');
const repositoryRoot = path.resolve(websiteRoot, '..');
const read = (relative: string): string =>
  readFileSync(path.join(repositoryRoot, relative), 'utf8');
const appPage = read('website/src/pages/app.astro');
const environmentExample = read('.env.example');
const buildSetup = read('website/tests/setup/build.ts');

const BUCKET_BASE = 'https://storage.googleapis.com/example-bucket/atlas/web/';

function dataBasesIn(html: string): { artifact: string; site: string } {
  const match =
    /<script[^>]*\bid="atlas-data-bases"[^>]*>([^<]*)<\/script>/.exec(html);
  expect(match, '#atlas-data-bases').not.toBeNull();
  return JSON.parse(match![1]!) as { artifact: string; site: string };
}

function astroBuild(base: string): string {
  const outDir = mkdtempSync(path.join(tmpdir(), 'genomeos-atlas-base-'));
  const environment: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = {
    ...process.env,
    ASTRO_TELEMETRY_DISABLED: '1',
    OUT_DIR: outDir,
    PUBLIC_ATLAS_DATA_BASE_URL: base,
  };
  delete environment.ATLAS_CATALOG_PATH;
  try {
    execFileSync(
      path.join(
        websiteRoot,
        'node_modules',
        '.bin',
        process.platform === 'win32' ? 'astro.cmd' : 'astro',
      ),
      ['build'],
      { cwd: websiteRoot, env: environment, stdio: 'pipe' },
    );
    return readFileSync(path.join(outDir, 'app', 'index.html'), 'utf8');
  } finally {
    rmSync(outDir, { force: true, recursive: true });
  }
}

describe('Atlas artifact data base wiring', () => {
  it('reads PUBLIC_ATLAS_DATA_BASE_URL only at the build boundary', () => {
    expect(appPage).toContain('import.meta.env.PUBLIC_ATLAS_DATA_BASE_URL');
    expect(appPage).toContain('id="atlas-data-bases"');
    expect(environmentExample).toMatch(/^PUBLIC_ATLAS_DATA_BASE_URL=$/m);
    expect(buildSetup).toContain("PUBLIC_ATLAS_DATA_BASE_URL: ''");
    expect(`${appPage}\n${environmentExample}\n${buildSetup}`).not.toMatch(
      /ATLAS_DATA_ORIGIN/,
    );
  });
});

describe('artifactDataBaseFrom', () => {
  it('falls back to the site base when unset or empty', () => {
    expect(artifactDataBaseFrom(undefined, '/data/atlas/')).toBe(
      '/data/atlas/',
    );
    expect(artifactDataBaseFrom('', '/genomeOS/data/atlas/')).toBe(
      '/genomeOS/data/atlas/',
    );
  });

  it('accepts the bucket base and the local fixture origin', () => {
    expect(artifactDataBaseFrom(BUCKET_BASE, '/data/atlas/')).toBe(
      BUCKET_BASE,
    );
    expect(artifactDataBaseFrom('http://127.0.0.1:4323/', '/data/atlas/')).toBe(
      'http://127.0.0.1:4323/',
    );
  });

  it.each([

```ts
/**
 * The artifact base for a build (design 2026-10-07 §C.1.4). `configured` is
 * `PUBLIC_ATLAS_DATA_BASE_URL`; empty or undefined means unset and falls back
 * to the same-origin site base (local development and tests only). A set value
 * must be an absolute URL ending in `/`: only the bucket base (or the local
 * fixture origin) may replace the site base, so root-relative values are refused.
 */
export function artifactDataBaseFrom(
  configured: string | undefined,
  siteDataBase: string,
): string {
  if (configured === undefined || configured === '') return siteDataBase;
  try {
    assertDataBase(configured);
  } catch (error) {
    throw new Error(
      `PUBLIC_ATLAS_DATA_BASE_URL ${JSON.stringify(configured)} is invalid: ${(error as Error).message}`,
    );
  }
  if (configured.startsWith('/'))
    throw new Error(
      `PUBLIC_ATLAS_DATA_BASE_URL must be an absolute URL ending in "/" (got ${JSON.stringify(configured)})`,
    );
  return configured;
}
```

import { mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { request, type IncomingHttpHeaders, type Server } from 'node:http';
import type { AddressInfo } from 'node:net';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import path from 'node:path';
import { gunzipSync } from 'node:zlib';

import { afterAll, beforeAll, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';

import { createAtlasDataServer } from '../scripts/serve-atlas-data.mjs';

const GRID = 'grids/h3-r3.0123456789abcdef.gosa';

let server: Server;
let port = 0;

function raw(
  pathName: string,
  headers: Record<string, string>,
  method = 'GET',
): Promise<{ status: number; headers: IncomingHttpHeaders; body: Buffer }> {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const outgoing = request(
      { host: '127.0.0.1', port, path: pathName, method, headers },
      (response) => {
        const chunks: Buffer[] = [];
        response.on('data', (chunk: Buffer) => chunks.push(chunk));
        response.on('end', () =>
          resolve({
            status: response.statusCode ?? 0,
            headers: response.headers,
            body: Buffer.concat(chunks),
          }),
        );
      },
    );
    outgoing.on('error', reject);
    outgoing.end();
  });
}

  writeFileSync(path.join(root, 'notes.txt'), 'not served');
  writeFileSync(path.join(parent, 'secret.json'), '{"outside":true}\n');

  port = (server.address() as AddressInfo).port;
});

afterAll(async () => {

});

    expect(response.headers['content-encoding']).toBe('gzip');
    expect(gunzipSync(response.body).toString()).toBe('GOSA fixture bytes');

- [ ] Step 3: Implement `website/scripts/serve-atlas-data.mjs`.

```js
/**
 * Serve a directory the way the public GCS bucket serves `atlas/web/` (design
 * 2026-10-07 §C.2, §C.3): gzip transport encoding when the client accepts it
 * (identity otherwise, like decompressive transcoding), the immutable
 * Cache-Control, and CORS grants only for origins in deploy/atlas-web-cors.json.
 * Playwright starts it on 127.0.0.1:4323 for the committed e2e tree (and for an
 * ATLAS_DATA_DIR staging tree in the performance harness), so browser tests
 * exercise absolute-URL resolution, crossorigin preload matching, CORS and
 * Content-Encoding.
 */
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { createServer } from 'node:http';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath, pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
import { parseArgs } from 'node:util';
import { gzipSync } from 'node:zlib';

const IMMUTABLE = 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable';
const CONTENT_TYPES = {
  '.gosa': 'application/octet-stream',
  '.json': 'application/json',
};
const CORS_FILE = fileURLToPath(
  new URL('../../deploy/atlas-web-cors.json', import.meta.url),
);

export function createAtlasDataServer({ root }) {
  const base = path.resolve(root);
  const [policy] = JSON.parse(readFileSync(CORS_FILE, 'utf8'));
  const origins = new Set(policy.origin);
  return createServer(async (request, response) => {
    const headers = { Vary: 'Origin' };
    const origin = request.headers.origin;
    if (origin && origins.has(origin)) {
      headers['Access-Control-Allow-Origin'] = origin;
      headers['Access-Control-Expose-Headers'] = policy.responseHeader.join(', ');
    }
    if (request.method === 'OPTIONS') {
      if (headers['Access-Control-Allow-Origin']) {
        headers['Access-Control-Allow-Methods'] = policy.method.join(', ');
        headers['Access-Control-Max-Age'] = String(policy.maxAgeSeconds);
      }
      response.writeHead(204, headers).end();
      return;
    }
    if (request.method !== 'GET' && request.method !== 'HEAD') {
      response.writeHead(405, headers).end();
      return;
    }
    let file;
    try {
      const pathname = decodeURIComponent(
        new URL(request.url ?? '/', 'http://fixture.invalid').pathname,
      );
      file = path.resolve(base, `.${pathname}`);
    } catch {
      response.writeHead(400, headers).end();
      return;
    }
    const type = CONTENT_TYPES[path.extname(file)];
    if (!type || !file.startsWith(`${base}${path.sep}`)) {
      response.writeHead(404, headers).end();
      return;
    }
    let body;
    try {
      body = await readFile(file);
    } catch {
      response.writeHead(404, headers).end();
      return;
    }
    const gzip = /\bgzip\b/.test(String(request.headers['accept-encoding'] ?? ''));
    const payload = gzip ? gzipSync(body, { level: 9 }) : body;
    headers['Cache-Control'] = IMMUTABLE;
    headers['Content-Type'] = type;
    headers['Content-Length'] = String(payload.length);
    if (gzip) headers['Content-Encoding'] = 'gzip';
    response.writeHead(200, headers);
    response.end(request.method === 'HEAD' ? undefined : payload);
  });
}

const invokedPath = process.argv[1]
  ? pathToFileURL(path.resolve(process.argv[1])).href
  : '';
if (import.meta.url === invokedPath) {
  const { values } = parseArgs({
    options: {
      root: { type: 'string' },
      host: { type: 'string', default: '127.0.0.1' },
      port: { type: 'string', default: '4323' },
    },
  });
  if (!values.root) throw new Error('--root is required');
  createAtlasDataServer({ root: values.root }).listen(
    Number(values.port),
    values.host,
    () =>
      console.log(
        `Atlas data ${path.resolve(values.root)} at http://${values.host}:${values.port}/`,
      ),
  );
}
```

/**
 * Cross-origin Atlas data (design 2026-10-07 §C.1.2, §C.3). The e2e build points
 * PUBLIC_ATLAS_DATA_BASE_URL at a second local origin (127.0.0.1:4323) that serves
 * the committed e2e tree with gzip and the bucket's CORS policy. Artifact objects
 * must come from that origin; Natural Earth borders, populated places and the
 * external caches must still come from the site.

import { expect, test, type Page, type Request } from '@playwright/test';

  [0, 0],

  [0, -18],

  [-18, -18],
  [18, -18],

  artifacts: {

}

async function inlineJson<T>(page: Page, id: string): Promise<T> {
  const value: unknown = await page
    .locator(`#${id}`)
    .evaluate((element) => JSON.parse(element.textContent ?? 'null'));
  return value as T;
}

function recordRequests(page: Page): Request[] {
  const requests: Request[] = [];
  page.on('request', (request) => requests.push(request));
  return requests;
}

async function preloadHrefs(page: Page): Promise<string[]> {
  return page
    .locator('link[rel="preload"][as="fetch"]')
    .evaluateAll((links) =>
      links.map((link) => (link as HTMLLinkElement).href),
    );
}

async function chooseAtlasMap(page: Page, id: string): Promise<void> {

    .getByRole('button', { name: /Select dataset\. Current dataset:/ })
    .click();

}

test('populated places and external caches stay on the site origin', async ({
  page,
  isMobile,
}) => {
  test.skip(
    isMobile,
    'coordinate-sensitive canvas picking is covered in the desktop project',
  );
  test.setTimeout(120_000);
  await page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' });
  const query = new URLSearchParams({
    heading: '0',
    height: '1000000',
    lat: '40.4407',
    lon: '-3.7201',
    pitch: '-90',
  });
  await page.goto(`/app/?${query}`);
  await expect(page.locator('[data-atlas-ready="true"]')).toBeVisible({
    timeout: 45_000,
  });
  const catalog = await inlineJson<InlineCatalog>(page, 'atlas-catalog');
  const places = catalog.context_sources.find(
    ({ id }) => id === 'natural-earth-populated-places',
  )!;
  const placesResponse = page.waitForResponse(
    (response) => response.url().endsWith(`/data/atlas/${places.url}`),
    { timeout: 60_000 },
  );

  await page
    .getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Inferred surface', exact: true })
    .uncheck();
  // Wait on state, not time: once the URL drops the surface layer, hovers can only land on
  // observations, whose preview is what fetches the populated places.
  await expect
    .poll(() => new URL(page.url()).searchParams.get('layers'))
    .not.toContain('surface');
  const canvas = page.locator('.atlas-scene canvas').first();
  const hoverPreview = page.locator('.atlas-hover-preview');
  const box = await canvas.boundingBox();
  expect(box).not.toBeNull();
  for (const [x, y] of OFFSETS) {
    await page.mouse.move(
      box!.x + box!.width / 2 + x,
      box!.y + box!.height / 2 + y,
    );
    if (await hoverPreview.isVisible()) break;
  }
  await expect(hoverPreview).toBeVisible();
  const placesFetched = await placesResponse;
  expect(new URL(placesFetched.url()).origin).toBe(SITE_ORIGIN);
  expect(placesFetched.status()).toBe(200);

  const hbs = catalog.artifacts.find(({ id }) => id === 'hbs-rs334')!;
  const externalResponse = page.waitForResponse(
    (response) =>
      hbs.external_resources.some(({ cache_url }) =>
        response.url().endsWith(`/data/atlas/${cache_url}`),
      ),
    { timeout: 60_000 },
  );
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'More info' }).click();
  const externalPanel = page.getByRole('complementary', {
    name: 'External variant information',
  });
  await expect(externalPanel).toBeVisible();
  await externalPanel.getByRole('button', { name: 'gnomAD' }).click();
  await expect(externalPanel).toContainText('Allele frequency');
  const external = await externalResponse;
  expect(new URL(external.url()).origin).toBe(SITE_ORIGIN);
  expect(external.status()).toBe(200);
});
```

specs pin `SITE_ORIGIN` to 4322, so the cross-origin specs pass only on the default port. To keep the

accept that origin; otherwise document that these specs need the default port.

the fixture must not answer those requests; builds with a same-origin base (`build:e2e` alone, which
the capture scripts use) keep the fixture's file fulfilment. Add after `extractInlineCatalog`:

```ts
const INLINE_CATALOG_TAG = /<script\b[^>]*\bid="atlas-catalog"[^>]*>/;

/** The artifact base baked into `#atlas-catalog`'s `data-artifact-data-base`, or null. */
export function extractArtifactDataBase(html: string): string | null {
  const tag = INLINE_CATALOG_TAG.exec(html)?.[0];
  return tag ? (/\bdata-artifact-data-base="([^"]*)"/.exec(tag)?.[1] ?? null) : null;
}
```

and in `installAtlasBrowserFixture`, directly after the `https://tile.openstreetmap.org/**` route,
wrap the e2e-object route so it is installed only for a same-origin base:

```ts
  const html = await (await page.request.get(options.appUrl ?? DEFAULT_APP_URL)).text();
  // design 2026-10-07 §C.3: an absolute artifact base is served by its own origin (webServer[1]).
  if (/^https?:\/\//.test(extractArtifactDataBase(html) ?? '')) return;
```

(the existing `await page.route((url) => keyFor(url) !== undefined, …)` follows unchanged).
`delayArtifactTier` and `failArtifactTier` already match by key suffix and end in `route.fallback()`
or `route.abort()`, so they work against either origin. `corruptArtifactTier` answers with
`route.fulfill`, and a fulfilled cross-origin response still has to pass CORS: in its `route.fulfill({
body, contentType: contentTypeFor(key), status: 200 })` call (and in the e2e-object route's
`route.fulfill`) add `headers: { 'access-control-allow-origin': '*' },` — the bucket's own policy
answers every listed origin, so the corrupted response differs from a real one only in its bytes.

`website/tests/support/atlas-data-target.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * Which data origin a built site's Atlas reads, for the performance harness
 * (design 2026-10-07 §C.3): the bucket (an absolute https base) or a local
 * staging tree served on 127.0.0.1:4323 from ATLAS_DATA_DIR. After Part C a
 * same-origin build has no per-artifact data, so it is refused loudly.
 */
export const LOCAL_DATA_BASE = 'http://127.0.0.1:4323/';

export type AtlasDataTarget =
  | { kind: 'bucket'; base: string }
  | { kind: 'local'; base: string; directory: string };

export function atlasDataTarget(
  appHtml: string,
  dataDirectory: string | undefined,
): AtlasDataTarget {
  const match =
    /<script[^>]*\bid="atlas-data-bases"[^>]*>([^<]*)<\/script>/.exec(appHtml);
  if (!match)
    throw new Error(
      'dist/app/index.html has no #atlas-data-bases element; run npm run build first',
    );
  const { artifact } = JSON.parse(match[1]!) as { artifact: string };
  if (artifact === LOCAL_DATA_BASE) {
    if (!dataDirectory)
      throw new Error(
        `this build reads Atlas data from ${LOCAL_DATA_BASE}; set ATLAS_DATA_DIR to a staging tree (encode_atlas_web.py --with-downloads --out DIR)`,
      );
    return { kind: 'local', base: artifact, directory: dataDirectory };
  }
  if (artifact.startsWith('https://')) return { kind: 'bucket', base: artifact };
  throw new Error(
    `this build reads Atlas data from ${JSON.stringify(artifact)}; rebuild with PUBLIC_ATLAS_DATA_BASE_URL set to the bucket base or ${LOCAL_DATA_BASE}`,
  );
}
```

const pagesWorkflow = read('.github/workflows/pages.yml');

function job(name: string): string {
  const start = pagesWorkflow.indexOf(`\n  ${name}:\n`);
  expect(start, `job ${name}`).toBeGreaterThan(-1);
  const rest = pagesWorkflow.slice(start + 1);
  const next = rest.search(/\n {2}[a-z-]+:\n/);
  return next < 0 ? rest : rest.slice(0, next);
}

describe('pages workflow', () => {
  it('sets the production base from the repository variable in the build job only', () => {
    const line = 'PUBLIC_ATLAS_DATA_BASE_URL: ${{ vars.ATLAS_DATA_BASE_URL }}';
    expect(pagesWorkflow.split(line)).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(job('build')).toContain(line);
    expect(pagesWorkflow).not.toMatch(/ATLAS_DATA_ORIGIN/);
  });

  it('gates validate (same-repository runs) and the production build on the published data', () => {
    expect(job('validate')).toContain(
      'python ../scripts/check_atlas_web_data.py --catalog public/data/atlas/catalog.json',
    );
    expect(job('validate')).toContain(
      'github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository',
    );
    const build = job('build');
    expect(build).toContain('python ../scripts/check_atlas_web_data.py --production');
    expect(build.indexOf('check_atlas_web_data.py')).toBeLessThan(
      build.indexOf('upload-pages-artifact'),
    );
  });

  it('refuses a production build without the variable or with a test catalog', () => {
    const build = job('build');
    expect(build).toContain('if [ -z "$PUBLIC_ATLAS_DATA_BASE_URL" ]; then');
    expect(build).toContain('if [ -n "${ATLAS_CATALOG_PATH:-}" ]; then');
    expect(
      build.indexOf('Refuse a production build without published Atlas data'),
    ).toBeLessThan(build.indexOf('Build production site'));
  });

  it('no longer encodes Atlas data in CI', () => {
    expect(pagesWorkflow).not.toContain('encode_atlas_web.py');
    expect(pagesWorkflow).not.toContain(

`website/src/content/docs/docs/deployment.md` — insert after the "## Build boundary" section:

```md
## Atlas data boundary

The Pages artifact carries the site, the Atlas catalog (inlined into `/app/`), the Natural Earth
context files and the `external/` caches. Per-artifact web data — the `.gosa` grid, render and detail
objects and the canonical surface, observations and manifest JSON — is served from a public Google
Cloud Storage bucket under immutable, content-addressed keys:

```text
atlas/web/grids/h3-r{resolution}.{sha256[:16]}.gosa
atlas/web/surfaces/{id}/{model_version}/{data_version}/{render|detail}.{sha256[:16]}.gosa
atlas/web/downloads/{id}/{model_version}/{data_version}/{id}.{surface|observations|manifest}.{sha256[:16]}.json
```

Objects are stored gzip-encoded with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, and their
decoded SHA-256 and size are object metadata. Downloads carry `Content-Disposition` so they save under
their canonical file names. Published objects are never replaced or deleted, because cached pages
keep referencing old keys.

The build reads the bucket base from `PUBLIC_ATLAS_DATA_BASE_URL`: an absolute `https://` URL that
ends in `atlas/web/`. The production build job takes it from the repository variable
`ATLAS_DATA_BASE_URL` and refuses to build without it; the deploy gate also reads the repository
variable `ATLAS_DATA_BUCKET`. Neither the bucket name nor the project is stored in the repository.

## Deploy gate

`scripts/check_atlas_web_data.py` runs before every deployment and on same-repository pull requests.
It refuses the deploy unless every object the catalog names answers with status 200,
`Content-Encoding: gzip`, the immutable `Cache-Control` and a CORS grant for each production origin;
its metadata records the catalog SHA-256 (and the decoded size wherever the catalog declares one); the
default map's grid, render tier and observations decompress to their catalog digests; and every
Natural Earth and external cache file is in the built site. A catalog that names objects before they
are published fails its deploy instead of shipping a broken map.
```

`website/src/content/docs/docs/local-development.md` — replace the whole "## Atlas web objects"

`tests/atlas-web-encode-ci.test.ts` pins):

```md
## Atlas data

The repository keeps the Atlas catalog, the Natural Earth context and the external caches.
Per-artifact data lives in the public bucket, so `npm run dev` needs a data base. Set
`PUBLIC_ATLAS_DATA_BASE_URL` in the repository-root `.env.development` (Vite reads `.env*` from the
repository root) to the bucket base — the value of the `ATLAS_DATA_BASE_URL` repository variable,
`https://storage.googleapis.com/<bucket>/atlas/web/` — or to `http://127.0.0.1:4323/` while
serving a local staging tree:

```bash
cd website
node scripts/serve-atlas-data.mjs --root /path/to/staging   # serves http://127.0.0.1:4323/
```

The tests do not need the bucket. `npm test` builds with the variable set to `''`, and
`npm run test:e2e` builds against `http://127.0.0.1:4323/` while Playwright serves the committed
fixture tree `tests/fixtures/atlas/e2e/` there with gzip and the bucket's CORS policy, so every
browser test exercises the cross-origin path.

Full-data checks are opt-in. `ATLAS_DATA_DIR` names a staging tree (written by
`encode_atlas_web.py --with-downloads --out DIR`, or downloaded from the bucket):

```bash
ATLAS_DATA_DIR=/path/to/staging npx vitest run tests/atlas-public-data.test.ts
ATLAS_DATA_DIR=/path/to/staging npx vitest run tests/atlas-geometry-full-grid.test.ts tests/atlas-render-precision.test.ts
PUBLIC_ATLAS_DATA_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4323/ npm run build
ATLAS_DATA_DIR=/path/to/staging npm run test:performance
```

The second line runs the full-grid chunk acceptance and the f32 precision report; both read the
surfaces through the staging tree's `catalog.json` `surface_url` and skip without data.

To measure against the bucket instead, build with the bucket base and run
`npm run test:performance` without `ATLAS_DATA_DIR`. The fixture-backed captures (`capture:atlas`,
`capture:atlas-mobile`, `capture:studs`) need no data base: they build the e2e catalog and the
browser fixture serves its objects. The full-data captures (`capture:progress`, `capture:gnomad`,
`capture:fast-load`) serve the built site on port 4323, so run them with
`PUBLIC_ATLAS_DATA_BASE_URL` set to the bucket base.

To publish new data, `export_atlas_web.py` output is an intermediate; the site build fails until
`encode_atlas_web.py` has run on it. Encode into a staging tree, publish it, and commit only its
catalog (see `docs/data-store.md`):

```bash
python scripts/encode_atlas_web.py --in <export-dir> --out data/atlas-web --with-downloads
```
```

`docs/deployment-gcp.md` — append:

```md
## Public Atlas web bucket

The website's per-artifact Atlas data (encoded `.gosa` tiers and the canonical surface,
observations and manifest JSON) is served from a separate **public** bucket. It is not the private
artifact bucket above and does not replace #33's artifact staging and version pinning: it holds only
encoded site data under content-addressed keys below `atlas/web/`.

- `us-east1`, uniform bucket-level access, `allUsers` with `roles/storage.objectViewer`, no object
  versioning (keys are content-addressed), default soft delete. Published objects are never deleted.
- CORS comes from `deploy/atlas-web-cors.json`: `GET` and `HEAD` from the production origins and the
  local ports 4321–4323.
- `python scripts/provision_atlas_web_bucket.py --mode edge` (provisioned) serves the objects from
  Google's edge cache at `https://storage.googleapis.com/<bucket>/atlas/web/`. `--mode cloud-cdn`
  (scripted, not provisioned) adds a backend bucket with Cloud CDN behind a global external HTTPS load
  balancer with a Google-managed certificate for `data.genome-os.org`; it needs a DNS A record at the
  registrar (a human step) and has a recurring load-balancer cost.
- Provisioning reads and reports public-access prevention and the effective
  `iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains`, `iam.managed.allowedPolicyMembers` and
  `storage.publicAccessPrevention` organization policies, and stops before changing anything when one
  would block public objects. It is idempotent and `--dry-run` prints every command.

The publish runbook is in [`data-store.md`](data-store.md#public-web-data-bucket).
```

`docs/data-store.md` — insert before "## Known gap":

```md
## Public web data bucket

The website's per-artifact data is published to a public bucket that is separate from #33's
private artifact staging: it serves only encoded site data and neither pins nor replaces the citable
artifacts above. Run the steps from a checkout, with the repository-local gcloud configuration
initialised first:

```bash
python scripts/gcloud_repo.py init --account <account> --project <project>
export GENOMEOS_GCP_PROJECT=<project> ATLAS_DATA_BUCKET=<bucket>
export ATLAS_DATA_BASE_URL="https://storage.googleapis.com/$ATLAS_DATA_BUCKET/atlas/web/"
python scripts/provision_atlas_web_bucket.py --mode edge --bucket "$ATLAS_DATA_BUCKET" --dry-run
python scripts/provision_atlas_web_bucket.py --mode edge --bucket "$ATLAS_DATA_BUCKET"
python scripts/encode_atlas_web.py --in <export-dir> --out data/atlas-web --with-downloads
python scripts/publish_atlas_web.py --staging data/atlas-web --bucket "$ATLAS_DATA_BUCKET" --dry-run
python scripts/publish_atlas_web.py --staging data/atlas-web --bucket "$ATLAS_DATA_BUCKET"
cp data/atlas-web/catalog.json website/public/data/atlas/catalog.json
gh variable set ATLAS_DATA_BUCKET --body "$ATLAS_DATA_BUCKET"
gh variable set ATLAS_DATA_BASE_URL --body "$ATLAS_DATA_BASE_URL"
(cd website && PUBLIC_ATLAS_DATA_BASE_URL="$ATLAS_DATA_BASE_URL" npm run build)
python scripts/check_atlas_web_data.py --production --catalog website/public/data/atlas/catalog.json \
    --base "$ATLAS_DATA_BASE_URL" --bucket "$ATLAS_DATA_BUCKET" --dist website/dist
```

`encode_atlas_web.py --with-downloads` copies each canonical JSON byte-for-byte to its
content-addressed `downloads/` key and rewrites `surface_url`, `observations_url` and
`downloads.*.url`; every SHA-256 is unchanged. Publishing compresses each file itself (gzip level 9,
mtime 0), uploads with `--if-generation-match=0`, and treats the decoded SHA-256 and size in object
metadata as identity: an identical object is skipped and a different one is a hard error, never an
overwrite, so a second run skips everything. The catalog commit comes last, after the deploy gate
passes against the bucket.

### Re-encoding after the per-artifact files left the repository

`main` tracks only `catalog.json`. To re-encode (after a codec change, say), first rebuild an export
tree, either with a full `scripts/export_atlas_web.py` run from the store, or by downloading the
published tree and adding the repository catalog (its keys already name the downloaded files):

```bash
python scripts/gcloud_repo.py run storage cp -r "gs://$ATLAS_DATA_BUCKET/atlas/web/*" <export-dir>/
cp website/public/data/atlas/catalog.json <export-dir>/catalog.json
(cd website && ATLAS_DATA_DIR=<export-dir> npx vitest run tests/atlas-public-data.test.ts)
```

The integrity test proves the download decompressed to the catalog's bytes. Then run
`encode_atlas_web.py --in <export-dir> --out <staging> --with-downloads`, publish, and copy only
`<staging>/catalog.json` back into the repository. The surface and observations JSON must stay
byte-identical: their SHA-256 values are in the catalog and in every citation, and a changed digest
is a new publication, not a re-encode. `scripts/build_atlas_e2e_fixture.py --from-dir <export-dir>`
regenerates the browser-test fixture from the same tree.
```

The objects are git-ignored; the JSON stays the citable download.") with: "It is
byte-deterministic. The objects are git-ignored; with `--with-downloads` they and the canonical JSON
are published to the public bucket (the "Public web data bucket" section below), the JSON stays the citable
download, and only `catalog.json` is committed."

## Part C operational tasks (Task 98 (C13)–Task 102 (C17), Task 103 (C19))

**These touch external systems** (the Google Cloud project, the public bucket, GitHub repository
settings). The owner authorised the agent to perform them on 2026-10-07 (spec §C.4.2). Rules for all
of them:

- Run from `$REPO` on `feat/atlas-gcs-web-data` with Tasks 86–97 committed **and Parts A and B
  merged to `main`** (spec §C.4: "Part B merged" comes before provisioning and publishing).
- **Hand-off after Task 97 (C12). Stop here.** Open the Part A, B and C PRs (C stacked on B). Do not
  start Tasks 98–104 until the owner has merged A and B: every object Task 100 (C15) publishes is
  public and never deleted, so publishing from an unmerged Part B would leave permanent orphans if
  Part B's review changes the codec, encoder or catalog. Task 98 (C13) Step 0 and Task 99 (C14) Step 0
  enforce this gate.
- `SCRATCH` is the executing session's scratchpad directory. The project id, bucket name and base URL
  live only in `$SCRATCH/atlas-web.env`; never in a tracked file, commit message or PR body
  (Plan ruling R20).
- Every gcloud call goes through `scripts/gcloud_repo.py` (directly or via the scripts).
- Nothing in the bucket is ever deleted. If a step reports a hard error, stop and report it.

```ts
/**
 * Published Atlas data (design 2026-10-07 §C.1.3, §C.3). The repository keeps
 * catalog.json, the Natural Earth context and the external caches; per-artifact
 * objects live in the public bucket. The catalog contract always runs. Set
 * ATLAS_DATA_DIR to a staging tree (encode_atlas_web.py --with-downloads --out
 * DIR, or a bucket download) to verify every published object.
 */
import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { existsSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

import { splitLongToH3Index } from 'h3-js';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';

import {
  atlasCatalogSchema,
  observationArtifactSchema,
  surfaceArtifactSchema,
} from '../src/atlas/contracts';
import {
  decodeDetail,
  decodeGrid,
  decodeRender,
} from '../src/atlas/gosa/decode';
import { populatedPlaceCatalogSchema } from '../src/atlas/place-context';

const siteData = fileURLToPath(new URL('../public/data/atlas/', import.meta.url));
const websiteRoot = fileURLToPath(new URL('..', import.meta.url));
const dataDirectory = process.env.ATLAS_DATA_DIR;

const POPULATED_ISLAND_CELLS = {
  Azores: '84351b5ffffffff',
  'Cook Islands': '84b4c59ffffffff',
  Madeira: '843466bffffffff',
  Malta: '843f305ffffffff',
  Praia: '845494bffffffff',
  Tenerife: '84344cdffffffff',
} as const;

const sha256 = (bytes: Uint8Array): string =>
  createHash('sha256').update(bytes).digest('hex');
const short = (digest: string): string => digest.slice(0, 16);
const arrayBuffer = (bytes: Buffer): ArrayBuffer =>
  bytes.buffer.slice(
    bytes.byteOffset,
    bytes.byteOffset + bytes.byteLength,
  ) as ArrayBuffer;
const catalog = atlasCatalogSchema.parse(
  JSON.parse(readFileSync(path.join(siteData, 'catalog.json'), 'utf8')),
);

describe('published Atlas catalog (repository copy)', () => {
  it('publishes validated public-domain city and region context', () => {
    const places = populatedPlaceCatalogSchema.parse(
      JSON.parse(
        readFileSync(path.join(siteData, 'ne-50m-populated-places.json'), 'utf8'),
      ),
    );
    expect(places.places.length).toBeGreaterThan(1_000);
    expect(places.places).toContainEqual(
      expect.objectContaining({
        country: 'Australia',
        name: 'Sydney',
        region: 'New South Wales',
      }),
    );
  });

  it('lists the thirty allowlisted maps on the shared resolution-4 WorldPop grid', () => {
    expect(catalog.artifacts).toHaveLength(30);
    const grids = Object.entries(catalog.grids);
    expect(grids).toHaveLength(1);
    const [gridSha256, grid] = grids[0]!;
    expect(grid.resolution).toBe(4);
    for (const reference of catalog.artifacts) {
      expect(reference.resolution, reference.id).toBe(4);
      expect(reference.target_grid_source, reference.id).toBe(
        'worldpop-1km-unconstrained',
      );
      expect(reference.target_grid_version, reference.id).toContain(
        'Global_2000_2020/2020/0_Mosaicked',
      );
      expect(reference.web.grid_sha256, reference.id).toBe(gridSha256);
      expect(reference.n_cells, reference.id).toBe(grid.n_cells);
      expect(reference.observations_available, reference.id).toBe(true);
      expect(reference.observations_bytes, reference.id).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    }
  });

  it('names every artifact object by the bucket layout and its content digest', () => {
    const [, grid] = Object.entries(catalog.grids)[0]!;
    expect(grid.url).toBe(
      `grids/h3-r${grid.resolution}.${short(grid.sha256)}.gosa`,
    );
    for (const reference of catalog.artifacts) {
      const prefix = `${reference.id}/${reference.model_version}/${reference.data_version}`;
      expect(reference.web.render.url).toBe(
        `surfaces/${prefix}/render.${short(reference.web.render.sha256)}.gosa`,
      );
      expect(reference.web.detail.url).toBe(
        `surfaces/${prefix}/detail.${short(reference.web.detail.sha256)}.gosa`,
      );
      for (const kind of ['manifest', 'observations', 'surface'] as const) {
        const download = reference.downloads[kind];
        expect(download, `${reference.id} ${kind}`).not.toBeNull();
        expect(download!.url).toBe(
          `downloads/${prefix}/${reference.id}.${kind}.${short(download!.sha256)}.json`,
        );
      }
      expect(reference.surface_url).toBe(reference.downloads.surface.url);
      expect(reference.downloads.surface.sha256).toBe(reference.surface_sha256);
      expect(reference.observations_url).toBe(
        reference.downloads.observations!.url,
      );
      expect(reference.downloads.observations!.sha256).toBe(
        reference.observations_sha256,
      );
    }
  });

  it('keeps site-base files in the Pages bundle and per-artifact files out of git', () => {
    for (const source of catalog.context_sources)
      expect(existsSync(path.join(siteData, source.url)), source.id).toBe(true);
    for (const reference of catalog.artifacts)
      for (const resource of reference.external_resources)
        expect(
          sha256(readFileSync(path.join(siteData, resource.cache_url))),
          resource.cache_url,
        ).toBe(resource.cache_sha256);
    const tracked = execFileSync('git', ['ls-files', 'public/data/atlas'], {
      cwd: websiteRoot,
      encoding: 'utf8',
    })
      .split('\n')
      .filter(Boolean);
    expect(
      tracked.filter((file) =>
        /\.(surface|observations|manifest)\.json$|\.gosa$/.test(file),
      ),
    ).toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe.skipIf(!dataDirectory)('published Atlas objects in ATLAS_DATA_DIR', () => {
  const read = (key: string): Buffer =>
    readFileSync(path.join(dataDirectory!, key));
  const checked = (object: {
    bytes: number;
    sha256: string;
    url: string;
  }): ArrayBuffer => {
    const bytes = read(object.url);
    expect(sha256(bytes), object.url).toBe(object.sha256);
    expect(bytes.byteLength, object.url).toBe(object.bytes);
    return arrayBuffer(bytes);
  };

  it('every object matches its digest, decodes, and aligns with the shared grid', () => {
    const [gridSha256, entry] = Object.entries(catalog.grids)[0]!;
    const grid = decodeGrid(checked(entry), { gridSha256, entry });
    const gridH3 = Array.from({ length: grid.n }, (_, row) =>
      splitLongToH3Index(grid.h3Lo[row]!, grid.h3Hi[row]!),
    );
    const gridCells = new Set(gridH3);
    for (const [island, h3Index] of Object.entries(POPULATED_ISLAND_CELLS))
      expect(gridCells.has(h3Index), island).toBe(true);

    for (const reference of catalog.artifacts) {
      const render = decodeRender(checked(reference.web.render), {
        ref: reference,
        grid,
      });
      decodeDetail(checked(reference.web.detail), {
        ref: reference,
        grid,
        render,
      });

      const surfaceBytes = read(reference.surface_url);
      expect(sha256(surfaceBytes), reference.id).toBe(reference.surface_sha256);
      const surface = surfaceArtifactSchema.parse(
        JSON.parse(surfaceBytes.toString('utf8')),
      );
      expect(surface.artifact.id, reference.id).toBe(reference.id);
      expect(surface.cells, reference.id).toHaveLength(reference.n_cells);
      expect(
        surface.cells.findIndex((cell, row) => cell.h3_index !== gridH3[row]),
        `${reference.id}: first row whose h3 differs from the grid`,
      ).toBe(-1);

      const observationBytes = read(reference.observations_url!);
      expect(sha256(observationBytes), reference.id).toBe(
        reference.observations_sha256,
      );
      expect(observationBytes.byteLength, reference.id).toBe(
        reference.observations_bytes,
      );
      const observations = observationArtifactSchema.parse(
        JSON.parse(observationBytes.toString('utf8')),
      );
      expect(observations.artifact.id, reference.id).toBe(reference.id);
      expect(observations.observations, reference.id).toHaveLength(
        reference.n_observations,
      );

      expect(sha256(read(reference.downloads.manifest.url)), reference.id).toBe(
        reference.downloads.manifest.sha256,
      );
    }

    // Moved from site.spec.ts: the complete default map (77,844 cells, 1,071 observations),
    // whose files the loop above has just parsed to these lengths.
    const hbs = catalog.artifacts.find(({ id }) => id === 'hbs-rs334')!;
    expect(hbs.n_cells).toBe(77_844);
    expect(hbs.n_observations).toBe(1_071);
  }, 900_000);
});
```
